Presidential Gubernatorial Nigeria’s Aviation Minister, Festus Keyamo
The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has given domestic airlines until 31 December to integrate their operations with the newly introduced Passenger Verification System (vPASS).
The minister warned that airlines that fail to comply will not be allowed to board passengers from 1 January 2027.
Mr Keyamo gave the directive on Monday during the official unveiling of the system at the General Aviation Terminal of the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos.
The system, introduced by the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), is designed to strengthen airport security, improve passenger processing and address identity fraud in domestic air travel.
Mr Keyamo said vPASS links passengers’ identities to their National Identification Numbers (NIN), allowing authorities to verify travellers before they gain access to departure lounges and board aircraft.
He said the technology would address practices such as airport touting, unauthorised access to departure lounges and the sale of flight tickets under false identities.
“It has eliminated touting at the airport where people, who have no business boarding aircraft, get access to the departure lounge, or they sell tickets to people in other names,” he said.

According to the minister, the system would also provide more accurate passenger manifests, making it easier for security agencies to establish the identities of people travelling on domestic flights.
He explained that the initiative is part of President Bola Tinubu’s plan to modernise the country’s airports through technology and private-sector investment.
Mr Keyamo said the Federal Executive Council approved the project in 2025, with implementation involving FAAN and private-sector investors.
He clarified that vPASS would initially apply to domestic flights, while a separate passenger identification arrangement for international travel had been developed in collaboration with the Ministry of Interior.
The minister said the system would first be deployed at airports in Lagos and Abuja before being extended to other domestic airports.
He also assured passengers that the private-sector partnership would not result in high additional costs, saying any charge associated with the system would be minimal.
The Managing Director of FAAN, Olubunmi Kuku, said vPASS would provide a single identification platform through which passengers could access different stages of airport processing using their NIN-linked information.
She explained that passengers who had completed registration could enter designated airport security gates by entering the last four digits of their NIN.
At airline boarding gates, passengers could be verified through facial or iris recognition, or by scanning QR codes on their boarding passes.
Ms Kuku said the technology would reduce the time spent on manual identity checks, improve operational efficiency and strengthen security within airport facilities.
She added that passengers could register at the airport or through applications available on iOS and Android devices.
According to her, Lagos and Abuja airports were ready for the initial rollout, while the period leading up to January would allow airlines and travellers to familiarise themselves with the technology before full implementation.
The Managing Director of VERXID Technologies Limited, Daniel Bankole, said his company was responsible for ensuring the smooth deployment of the system, protecting passengers’ data and complying with relevant data protection laws.
He said the objective was to provide passengers with a secure and efficient experience across the airport system.
The Director-General of the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC), Jobson Ewalefoh, said the project had undergone the required approval and regulatory processes, including clearance by the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation.
Mr Ewalefoh described the initiative as an important addition to Nigeria’s security architecture, saying access to reliable passenger information would improve the identification of people travelling by air.
He added that the commission would continue to monitor compliance with the obligations and commitments under the private-sector partnership.
PREMIUM TIMES had reported in April that the Federal Government approved the deployment of a contactless biometric passenger verification system across Nigeria’s domestic airports as part of efforts to strengthen aviation security and improve passenger data management.
Mr Keyamo had announced the approval after signing a concession agreement for the implementation of the vPASS system.
The government said the technology would address inconsistencies in passenger records, prevent unauthorised boarding, and close gaps in identifying travellers on domestic flights.
In July, FAAN also announced plans to deploy the system in partnership with VERXID Technologies Limited, explaining that passengers would undergo a one-time registration process using their NIN and biometric details.
The latest unveiling marks another step toward implementing the system, with the December deadline now setting a compliance timeline for domestic airlines.
However, the initial rollout will be limited to Lagos and Abuja before expansion to other domestic airports across the country.
